en: negative example to learn from; cautionary example

examples.ko: 그 실수를 반면교사로 삼아 다시는 안 해요.
examples.en: I use that mistake as a lesson and never do it again.
I prepared, taking my senior's failure as a negative example.

examples.ko: 이 사례는 반면교사가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: This case can serve as a lesson on what not to do.

examples.ko: 나쁜 습관을 가진 친구는 제게 반면교사였어요.
examples.en: A friend with bad habits was a cautionary example for me.
This accident is a good example of learning from what went wrong.

examples.ko: 싸우는 모습을 보고 반면교사라는 말을 떠올렸어요.
examples.en: Seeing them fight, I remembered the word 'banmyeongyosa'.

explain: '반면교사로 삼다' 꼴로 거의 굳어서 써요. '타산지석'은 남의 좋은 말과 행동에서도 배울 때 쓰지만, '반면교사'는 나쁜 모습에만 써요. 따라 배울 좋은 본보기는 '귀감'이에요.

phrases.en: I took my friend's mistake as a lesson on what not to do.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 단어가 거의 굳어서 쓰이는 대표적인 꼴이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The set phrase in which this word is almost always used.
phrases.en_equiv: to take as a cautionary lesson

phrases.example: 그 사고를 반면교사 삼아 안전 점검을 했어요.
phrases.en: Taking that accident as a cautionary lesson, we did a safety check.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '로'를 빼고 연결형으로 쓰는 말투로, 글과 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form without '로' and in connective style, common in writing and news.

phrases.example: 그의 실패가 우리에게 좋은 반면교사가 됐어요.
phrases.en: His failure became a good cautionary example for us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 나쁜 모습이 배울 거리가 된다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that someone else's bad example becomes something to learn from.
phrases.en_equiv: to become a good negative example

explain_en: It is nearly fixed in the form '반면교사로 삼다'. '타산지석' can also be used when learning from others' good words and actions, but '반면교사' is used only for bad examples. A good example to follow is '귀감'.

en: to become proficient; to become adept

examples.en: Becoming proficient takes repetition more than tricks.

examples.ko: 운전은 숙달이 빠른 사람도 있고 느린 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: With driving, some people get proficient quickly and others slowly.
If you practice every day, your hands get skilled quickly.
A skilled cook is really fast with a knife.

examples.ko: 처음엔 어려웠지만 몇 달 지나니 일이 숙달됐어요.
examples.en: It was hard at first, but after a few months I got the hang of the work.

examples.ko: 기계 사용법이 숙달될 때까지 천천히 해 보세요.
examples.en: Take it slowly until you get used to operating the machine.

explain: 일상에서는 '익숙해지다'가 더 흔하고, '숙달되다'는 기술이나 동작을 반복해서 능숙해졌을 때 써요. '숙달된 조교'처럼 '숙달된 + 명사' 형태로 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Thanks to the well-practiced skill, the work is fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반복해서 능숙해진 기술을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a skill made proficient by repetition.

phrases.en: I practice every day until I become proficient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능숙해질 때까지 계속한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means continuing until you become skilled.

phrases.en: I gradually got used to the new job.
phrases.nuance_ko: '숙달되다'보다 일상에서 흔하고 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common and lighter in everyday speech than '숙달되다'.

explain_en: To get familiar with a skill through practice, more neutral. In daily talk '익숙해지다' is more common; '숙달되다' is for becoming skilled at a technique or movement through repetition. It often appears in the form '숙달된 + noun', like '숙달된 조교' (a skilled assistant).

t90.ax: A skilled cook is really fast with a knife.

en: the fate of having loads of work

examples.ko: 저는 일복을 타고났는지 쉬는 날에도 일이 생겨요.
examples.en: I must be born with a fate of endless work; even on days off, work comes up.

examples.ko: 올해는 일복이 터져서 야근을 매일 해요.
examples.en: Work is piling up on me this year, so I work overtime every day.

examples.ko: 일복 많은 사람은 휴가 중에도 회사 전화를 받아요.
examples.en: People with loads of work even take calls from the office on vacation.
They say the team leader has loads of work but his pay stays the same.

examples.ko: 사주에 일복도 많다고 하더니 정말 바쁘네요.
examples.en: They said my fortune had lots of work in it, and I really am busy.

examples.ko: 일복에 치여 사는 친구에게 맛있는 걸 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I bought something tasty for my friend who is buried in work.

explain: '복'이 붙었지만 좋은 운이 아니라 일이 끊이지 않는 팔자를 농담처럼 투덜거리며 말할 때 써요. '일복이 많다/터지다/타고나다'로 자주 말하고, '인복', '식복'처럼 '~복'이 붙는 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I'm swamped with work these days, so I go in even on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 한꺼번에 몰려 정신없이 바쁠 때 농담처럼 불평하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking complaint for when work piles up all at once and you are frantically busy.

explain_en: It has '복' (luck) in it, but it is not good luck; people use it jokingly, with a grumble, for a fate of never-ending work. It is usually said as '일복이 많다/터지다/타고나다', and it is easy to remember together with words like '인복' and '식복'.

en: to get ahead in life; to rise in the world

examples.en: My mother hopes that I will get far in life.
He came up from the countryside and made it big in Seoul.

examples.ko: 출세하려고 윗사람에게만 잘 보이는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people only try to please their superiors in order to get ahead.

examples.ko: 저는 친구에게 빨리 출세해서 부럽다고 말했어요.
examples.en: I told my friend that I envy how quickly he rose in the world.

examples.ko: 출세한 뒤에도 고향 친구들을 잊지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after becoming successful, he didn't forget his hometown friends.

examples.ko: 출세하는 것보다 행복하게 사는 게 더 중요해요.
examples.en: Living happily is more important than getting ahead.

explain: '성공하다'는 일이 잘되는 것 전반을 말하지만, '출세하다'는 사회적으로 높은 지위나 좋은 직업을 얻는 쪽에 가까워요. 지위 욕심이 느껴질 때도 있어서 '출세주의'처럼 부정적인 말에도 나와요.

phrases.en: I want to get ahead in life quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 지위를 얻고 싶다는 바람을 말하는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form expressing the wish to gain a high position.

phrases.en: In his hometown, they call him a man who made it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사회적으로 성공한 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to refer to someone who succeeded socially.

phrases.en: He rose quickly in the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '출세'를 써서 승진이 빠르다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '출세' to mean one's career advanced fast.

explain_en: '성공하다' covers things going well in general, while '출세하다' is closer to reaching a high social position or a good career. It can hint at ambition for status, so it also appears in negative words like '출세주의' (careerism).

examples.en: I felt heavy-hearted after hearing the teacher's admonishment.

examples.ko: 아버지는 긴 훈계 끝에 아들을 용서했어요.
examples.en: After a long lecture, the father forgave his son.
I don't like to listen to preaching that sounds like nagging.
My younger brother came late again despite the warning.
Grandmother gave her grandson a short word of caution.

examples.ko: 훈계만 하지 말고 이유도 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't just lecture me, but listen to my reasons too.

explain: 부모님이나 선생님 같은 윗사람이 잘못을 고치도록 타이르는 말에 써요. '잔소리'는 듣는 사람이 귀찮아하는 느낌이 강하고, '꾸중'은 이미 한 잘못을 혼내는 쪽에 가까워요. 보통 '훈계를 하다/듣다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: I quietly listened to my father's admonishment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 훈계를 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person being admonished.

phrases.en: The teacher gave the students a talking-to.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 타이르는 행동을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for a superior's act of admonishing.

phrases.en: Please don't talk in a preachy tone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가르치려는 듯한 말투를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a lecturing, preachy tone of voice.

explain_en: It is used when someone senior, like a parent or teacher, talks to you to correct your behavior. '잔소리' (nagging) carries an annoyed feeling, and '꾸중' (scolding) is closer to being told off for something you already did. It is usually used as '훈계를 하다/듣다'.

t90.ax: After a long lecture, the father forgave his son.

en: idiom derived from a classical story or historical event

examples.en: Do you know the origin of this idiom?
Many Chinese-character idioms appear on the exam.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 말씀하실 때 고사성어를 자주 쓰세요.
examples.en: My grandfather often uses idioms when he speaks.

examples.ko: 오늘 수업에서 새로운 고사성어 세 개를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In class today I learned three new idioms.
If you know idioms, it is easier to understand writing.
Idioms like these carry old stories inside them.

explain: 옛이야기에서 나온 말이라 '사자성어'와 조금 달라요. 보통 한자 네 글자로 되어 있지만 이야기가 있는 말을 가리켜요. 글이나 말에 넣으면 점잖고 지식 있는 느낌이 나요.

phrases.en: I memorize one idiom a day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고사성어'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 공부할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing with 고사성어, often used when studying.

phrases.en: What does this idiom mean?
phrases.nuance_ko: 모르는 말을 물어볼 때 조사 '의'를 붙여 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the particle 의 when asking about an unfamiliar idiom.

phrases.example: 사자성어를 많이 알면 글쓰기에 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: Knowing many four-character idioms helps with writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한자 네 글자로 된 말 전체를 가리키고, 꼭 옛이야기에서 나온 말만은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to any four-character idiom, not only those from old stories.

explain_en: It differs a bit from '사자성어' (four-character phrase) because it comes from an old story. It is usually four Chinese characters, but refers to one with a story behind it. Using one in speech or writing gives a polished, learned feeling.

examples.ko: 1988년 서울 올림픽에서 굴렁쇠를 굴리는 아이가 화제였어요.
examples.en: At the 1988 Seoul Olympics, the child rolling a hoop became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 어릴 때 굴렁쇠를 굴리며 놀았대요.
examples.en: I heard Grandfather played rolling a hoop when he was little.
I tried rolling a hoop at the folk village.

examples.ko: 굴렁쇠가 넘어지지 않게 막대로 살살 밀어 보세요.
examples.en: Push the hoop gently with the stick so it doesn't fall over.

examples.ko: 요즘 아이들은 굴렁쇠를 거의 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: Kids these days have hardly ever seen a hoop like that.

examples.ko: 굴렁쇠처럼 둥근 바퀴가 언덕 아래로 굴러갔어요.
examples.en: A round wheel like a hoop rolled down the hill.

explain: 아이들이 막대로 굴리며 놀던 둥근 테를 가리키는 옛 놀이 도구 이름이에요. 한국 사람들은 1988년 서울 올림픽 개막식에서 한 소년이 굴렁쇠를 굴리던 장면으로도 많이 기억해요.

phrases.en: The child rolls the hoop with a stick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굴렁쇠와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with 굴렁쇠.

phrases.en: I tried the hoop game at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 아이들이 하던 놀이 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the traditional children's game.

phrases.en: The hoop boy scene is still famous today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 1988년 올림픽 개막식의 그 소년을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name for the boy in the 1988 Olympic opening ceremony.

explain_en: It is the name of an old toy: a round hoop that children rolled along with a stick. Many Koreans also remember it from the opening ceremony of the 1988 Seoul Olympics, where a boy rolled one across the stadium.

examples.ko: 옛이야기 속 도깨비방망이는 두드리면 뭐든 나와요.
examples.en: In old tales, anything comes out when you knock the goblin's club.

examples.ko: 도깨비방망이가 있다면 먼저 집을 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: If I had a goblin's magic club, I'd make a house first.
The child plays swinging a stick like a goblin's club.
There is no magic-wand solution in this world.
In the storybook, gold poured out when the goblin's club was struck.

examples.ko: 도깨비방망이를 갖고 싶다고 말하는 아이가 많아요.
examples.en: Many children say they want a goblin's magic club.

explain: 전래동화에서 도깨비가 가진 방망이로, 두드리면 원하는 것이 나와요. 지금은 '도깨비방망이 같은 해결책'처럼 한 번에 다 해결해 줄 것 같은 만능 방법을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 도깨비방망이 같은 해결책을 찾지 말고 하나씩 해 봐요.
phrases.en: Don't look for a magic-wand solution; let's try one thing at a time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단번에 문제를 해결해 줄 것 같은 만능 방법을 말해요. 보통 그런 방법은 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means an all-purpose fix that seems to solve a problem at once. It is usually used to say that no such fix exists.

explain_en: This is the club that goblins hold in folktales, and whatever you wish for comes out when you strike it. Today it is also used in phrases like '도깨비방망이 같은 해결책' for an all-purpose fix that seems to solve everything at once.

examples.en: Cafés with a retro vibe are popular these days.
Retro designs are in fashion again.
This song has a strong retro feel.
They decorated the inside of the shop in a retro style.
That outfit is retro, so older people like it too.

examples.ko: 복고적 취향이라 옛날 노래를 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I have retro tastes, so I often listen to old songs.

explain: 옛날 스타일을 다시 살린 느낌을 말해요. '레트로'라고도 하고, 비슷한 말로 '복고풍'이 있어요. 패션, 음악, 인테리어 이야기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I bought clothes with a retro feel.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인' 모양으로 명사를 꾸며요. 옛날 스타일의 분위기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-인' form modifies a noun, describing an old-style vibe.

phrases.en: Retro-style songs are popular again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말이에요. '복고적'보다 명사로 바로 붙여 쓰기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that attaches more easily directly to nouns than '복고적'.

phrases.en: The retro-style bag is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍고 편한 말투에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used a lot in casual, light speech.

explain_en: It describes a feel that revives an old style. People also say '레트로', and a similar word is '복고풍'. It is common in talk about fashion, music and interior design.

t90.ax: This song has a strong retro feel.

examples.en: On the morning of the first full moon, I cracked and ate bureom nuts.
Grandmother prepared walnuts and peanuts for bureom.

examples.ko: 올해는 부럼도 사 놓고 오곡밥도 지었어요.
examples.en: This year I bought bureom nuts and also made five-grain rice.
At the supermarket, bureom nuts were sold as sets.

examples.ko: 부럼 깨기는 정월 대보름의 대표적인 풍습이에요.
examples.en: Cracking bureom nuts is a typical custom of the first full moon.

examples.ko: 오곡밥과 부럼과 나물을 차려 놓고 보름을 보냈어요.
examples.en: We spent the full moon with five-grain rice, bureom nuts and seasoned greens set out.

explain: 정월 대보름 아침에 깨물어 먹는 호두, 땅콩, 밤 같은 단단한 견과를 말해요. '부럼 깨기'라고 하고, 한 해 동안 부스럼이 나지 않기를 바라며 이로 딱 소리 나게 깨물어요.

phrases.example: 할머니와 같이 부럼을 깨물고 소원을 빌었어요.
phrases.en: I cracked the nuts with my grandmother and made a wish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이로 딱 깨무는 행동을 말할 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most natural when describing biting the nuts with your teeth.
phrases.en_equiv: to crack nuts with your teeth

phrases.example: 우리 가족은 해마다 부럼 깨기를 해요.
phrases.en: My family cracks nuts every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대보름 풍습의 이름으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the custom on the full moon day.

phrases.en: There is a custom of eating nuts on the first full moon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍습을 설명할 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase for explaining the custom.

explain_en: It refers to hard nuts like walnuts, peanuts and chestnuts that people crack and eat on the morning of the first full moon. The custom is called '부럼 깨기', and people bite them with a crack, hoping not to get skin boils through the year.

examples.en: My father often listens to trot music in the car.
My friend sang old trot songs with gusto at karaoke.
Do young people these days like trot too?
Trot music is blaring out of the market.

examples.ko: 할머니가 뽕짝 리듬에 맞춰 어깨를 흔드셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma swayed her shoulders to the trot rhythm.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 뽕짝 느낌이 나서 정겨워요.
examples.en: This song has a trot feel, so it feels warm and familiar.

explain: 트로트를 편하게, 조금 옛날식으로 부르는 말이에요. 말투에 따라 가볍게 보는 느낌이 있을 수 있어서, 격식 있는 자리에서는 '트로트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother likes trot music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 음악을 가리키는 보통 쓰는 말로, 격식 있는 자리에서도 괜찮아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The standard name for the same music, fine in formal settings too.

phrases.en: When I hear trot songs, my shoulders start to bounce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 편한 사이에서 쓰는 말투로, 옛날 트로트 곡을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual expression often used for old-style trot songs.

phrases.en: A trot medley was playing in the taxi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 곡을 이어서 부르거나 들려주는 걸 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for several trot songs strung together.

explain_en: It is a casual, slightly old-fashioned way to say '트로트' (trot). Depending on tone it can sound a bit dismissive, so in formal settings people say '트로트'.

examples.en: Since retiring, I tend a small garden as a pastime.
My grandfather is bored because he has nothing to pass the time.
Knitting is a good way for me to pass the time.
Try finding even a small pastime to get through the day.

examples.ko: 용돈도 벌 수 있는 소일거리를 구하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a light job that also earns some pocket money.
I go fishing every weekend to pass the time.

explain: 큰 목적 없이 시간을 보내려고 하는 가벼운 일을 말해요. '취미'보다 가볍고, 은퇴한 분이나 시간이 남는 사람의 작은 일에 잘 어울려요. '소일거리 삼아'라는 말투로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 소일거리 삼아 매일 아침 산책을 해요.
phrases.en: I take a walk every morning as a way to pass the time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 시간 보내는 용도로 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you do something as a way to pass time.

phrases.en: My retired father is looking for something to keep himself busy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 보낼 가벼운 일을 구한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means looking for a light activity to fill time.

phrases.en: I do puzzles just to kill time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소일거리'와 비슷하지만 지루함을 달래는 느낌이 더 강하고 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 소일거리 but more casual, with a feel of chasing away boredom.

explain_en: It means a light activity you do just to pass the time, without any big purpose. It is lighter than '취미' (hobby) and suits small things done by retirees or people with spare time. The phrase '소일거리 삼아' (as a way to pass the time) is a common pattern.

examples.en: That soprano's voice is really clear.
My sister took the soprano part in the choir.
A famous soprano is performing in Seoul.
Sopranos sing the high notes.
Alto is more comfortable for me than soprano.
In the opera, the soprano and the tenor sang together.

explain: 여자 목소리 중 가장 높은 음역을 말해요. 낮은 쪽은 '알토', 남자 높은 목소리는 '테너'라고 해요. 합창에서는 '소프라노 파트'처럼 파트 이름으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 저는 소프라노 가수의 공연을 보러 가요.
phrases.en: I'm going to see a soprano singer's performance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목소리 높이가 아니라 노래하는 사람을 말할 때 뒤에 '가수'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 가수 to talk about the singer, not just the voice range.

phrases.en: I practice the soprano part in the choir.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합창에서 높은 소리를 내는 부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the highest vocal part in a choir.

phrases.en: She sings as a soprano.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 음역으로 노래하는지 말할 때 '-로'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use -로 to say which vocal range someone sings in.

explain_en: It is the highest range of the female voice. The lower female part is 알토, and the high male voice is 테너. In choirs people often say it as a part name, like 소프라노 파트.

examples.ko: 주말에 집에서 쉬는 게 저한테는 신선놀음이에요.
examples.en: Resting at home on weekends is pure bliss to me.

examples.ko: 월급 받으면서 이렇게 노니 신선놀음이 따로 없어요.
examples.en: Getting paid while loafing like this, it couldn't be more carefree.

examples.ko: 신선놀음에 빠져 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I got lost in leisurely fun and didn't notice the time.

examples.ko: 바둑 두며 보내는 오후가 신선놀음 같아요.
examples.en: An afternoon spent playing baduk feels like a carefree idyll.

examples.ko: 휴가 내내 신선놀음만 했더니 몸이 근질근질해요.
examples.en: I only lounged around the whole vacation, and now I'm itching to move.
If you keep lazing around like that, your work will pile up.

explain: 신선처럼 걱정 없이 편하게 노는 모습을 부러워하거나, 일은 안 하고 한가하다고 핀잔할 때 둘 다 써요. 어떤 뜻인지는 말투와 상황으로 알 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 게임에 빠져 하루가 다 갔어요, 신선놀음에 도낏자루 썩는 줄 모른다더니.
phrases.en: A whole day went by in the game, just like the saying about losing track of time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미있는 일에 푹 빠지면 시간이 가는 줄 모른다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that when you are absorbed in something fun, you lose track of time.
phrases.en_equiv: Time flies when you're having fun

explain_en: It can express envy at someone carefree like an immortal sage, or tease someone for idling instead of working. Tone and situation tell you which meaning is intended.
